Title: A Clerk of Oxford
Description: Personal blog of Eleanor Parker (University of Oxford), who is interested in the literature and history of medieval England, with its saints, churches, folklore, Vikings, and poetry.

Title: A Thesaurus of Old English
Description: Conceptually arranged thesaurus of the vocabulary of Anglo-Saxon England. Within ordered categories, it provides information about word meaning resembling an inside-out dictionary (first the meanings and then the words). Created by the University of Glasgow.

Title: Beowulf on steorarume
Description: Digital edition of Beowulf with a PDE translation along the original OE text, with supplementary texts and PDE translations of The Fight at Finnsburh, Waldere, DeorWoden's Nine Herbs Charm, and Bede's Account of Cædmon. The website provides explanatory notes on the text and audio recordings in OE of selected passages. Created by Benjamin Slade.

Title: Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary
Description: Online Old English dictionary." The project is based on a digital edition of An Anglo-Saxon dictionary, based on the manuscript collections of the late Joseph Bosworth (the so called Main Volume, first edition 1898) and its Supplement (first edition 1921), edited by Joseph Bosworth and T. Northcote Toller, today the largest complete dictionary of Old English. Maintained by Ondrej Tichy and Martin Rocek (Charles University of Prague).

Title: Cambridge Digital Library
Description: Collection of the digital editions of the manuscripts housed in the Cambridge University Library.

Title: Dictionary of Old English website and corpus
Description: Dictionary of Old English, based on a computerized Corpus comprising at least one copy of each text surviving in Old English and providing parsed lists of all attested spellings, grammatical information, and detailed sense divisions (supported by illustrative citations from the Corpus) for each word. Created by the University of Toronto. Subscription is required for access to the dictionary and corpus.

Title: Digitised Manuscripts (British Library)
Description: Collection of the digital editions of the manuscripts housed in the British Library.

Title: Early English Laws
Description: Digital and printed new editions and translations of all English legal codes, edicts, and treatises produced up to the time of Magna Carta 1215.Created by the University of St Andrews.

Title: Electronic Beowulf 5.0
Description: Digital edition of Beowulf closely based on the original text.with images of all the early transcripts and collations of the manuscript. The edition restores original text through ultraviolet images and digitized backlighting to reveal erased or faded readings and the use of chemical reagents.Created by Kevin Kiernan, editor and designer, and Emil Iacob, software engineer (University of Kentucky, Georgia Southern University).

Title: EM1060: The Production and Use of English Manuscripts 1060-1220
Description: Record of manuscripts written principally in English from c. 1060 to 1220, with descriptions and occasional digital images. An accompanying e-book provides in-depth discussions of the manuscripts containing English vernacular. Created by Stanford University.

Title: English Place-Name Society
Description: Society which conducts a county-by-county survey of the place-names of England. Members receive the current issue of the Journal as well as the volume of the Survey allocated to that year's subscription.

Title: Essentials of Old English
Description: Manual of OE grammar with exercises, devided into Orthography and Pronunciation, Syntax, and Paradigms. Designed for beginners of OE with previous knowledge of basic PDE grammar and phonetics. An app version is also available. Created by the University of Glasgow.

Title: Fontes Anglo-Saxonici: A Register of Written Sources Used by Anglo-Saxon Authors
Description: Database register that aims to identify all written sources which were incorporated, quoted, translated, or adapted in English or Latin texts that were (likely) written in Early Medieval England, including those by foreign authors.The database includes about 1150 Anglo-Saxon texts, over 500 in Old English and over 600 in Latin.

Title: For the Wynn
Description: Personal blog of Kate Thomas (University of York), who is interested in Anglo-Saxon prayer, liturgy, medicine, and manuscript studies.

Title: Fritz Stieleke's YouTube Channel
Description: YouTube channel with AI-generated neo-Old English songs. Created by Fritz Stieleke (Heinrich-Heyne Universität Düsseldorf)

Title: Germanic Lexicon Project
Description: Collection of digitized texts related to the early Germanic languages, with scanned image files. Includes A Concise Anglo-Saxon Dictionary by John R. Clark Hall (1916) and An Anglo-Saxon Reader by James W. Bright (1912). Parts of the work on An Anglo-Saxon Dictionary by Joseph Bosworth and T. Northcote Toller (1898 and 1921) later became the Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary. Created by Sean Crist.

Title: Hwider … ðū? Gap-Filling Exercises for the Old English Class
Description: Exercise book with gap-fills, with sentences from OE texts illustrated by pictures of modern surroundings. A focus is placed on acquiring elementary OE morphology through the illusion of OE as a present-day language. Created by Fritz Stieleke ( Heinrich-Heine-Universität).

Title: International Society for the Study of Early Medieval England
Description: Organisation for those interested in history, art, archaeology, literature, languages, religion, society, and numismatics of England between the years c. 450 and 1100 CE. The organisation oversees biennial conferences, running graduate workshops, awarding publication prizes, sponsoring “New Voices” sessions at the Kalamazoo and Leeds medieval conferences for early-career scholars, and maintaining the ISSEME mailing list.

Title: Introducing Old English
Description: YouTube videos presenting an overview of OE grammar. Created by Alaric Hall (University of Leeds).

Title: Junicode font
Description: Short for Junius-Unicode, the Junicode is a TrueType/OpenType font for medievalists, free of charge under the Open font License. It provides extensive coverage of the Latin Unicode ranges, plus Runic and Gothic, and the font comes in four faces.

Title: King Alfred's Grammar
Description: Electronic textbook on Old English with grammar exercises, translation and reading practices. Created by Michael D. C. Drout (Wheaton College)

Title: Medieval Fleming
Description: Personal blog of Damian Fleming (Purdue University Fort Wayne).

Title: Nerthus Project: Online Lexical Database of Old English
Description: Project which implements a language model for OE based on a natural language processing (NLP) library adjusted for morphosyntactic annotation with Universal Dependencies (UD), in order to automatically annotate a corpus of Old English prose consisting of 300,000 words. Created by the Universidad de La Rioja.

Title: Nū ġē lā! A Pictorial Invitation to Old English
Description: Teaching manual with a selection of sentences from Ælfric's Grammar paired with present-day photographs. Created by Fritz Stieleke (Heinrich-Heine-Universität).

Title: Old English Aerobics
Description: Anthology, Glossary and Workout Room. Supplementary materials to Peter S. Baker's Introduction to Old English, with online versions of all the texts in the book’s anthology, interactive exercises, and a glossary. Created by the University of Virginia.

Title: Old English Core Vocabulary
Description: List of c. 600 OE literary core vocabulary words. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Core Vocabulary St Andrews Flashcards
Description: Digital flashcards of OE core vocabulary with free access on Quizlet. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Grammar
Description: Digital companion to Murray McGillivray’s Gentle Introduction to Old English with hypertext versions of the book’s texts, interactive grammar exercises, and outlines of OE grammar. Created by Murray McGillivray.

Title: Old English Grammar Bytes
Description: Bite-size videos on Old English grammar, specifically cases, adjectives, verbs and nouns. Created by Thijs Porck (Leiden University)

Title: Old English grammar exercises at ASNC Spoken Word
Description: Beginner and advanced OE grammar and translation exercises. Created by the University of Cambridge.

Title: Old English Martyrology: An Annotated Bibliography
Description: Bibliography of publications on the Old English Martyrology. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Newsletter Archives
Description: Free archived volumes of the Old English Newsletter. Published by The University of Massachusetts, Amherst.

Title: Old English Online
Description: Website designed to help users learn to read Old English. Each module covers a major grammar concept and is accompanied by interactive exercises (vocabulary flashcards, fill-in-the-blank grammar quizzes with tailored explanatory feedback, reading comprehensions with optional glosses, notes, and translations). Created by Tom Birkett with Victoria Koivisto-Kokko (University College Cork).

Title: Old English Poetry in Facsimile
Description: A collaborative, open-access resource of digital facsimile editions of OE poetry, linking digital manuscript images, transcriptions, editorial annotations, and translations. OEPF builds on the foundation of the Anglo-Saxon Poetic Records (1932-1953), while adding a new and digital edition of record and reference, updated materials, scholarly citations, and methodologies. Editions practice "restorative retention." The project employs the new Digital Mappa 3.0 platform, which allows editors to make links and annotations across individual moments on related images and texts, and users to open and view multiple items side by side. Created by Martin Foys with Kyle Smith and contributing editors (Digital Mappa).

Title: Old English Wordhord
Description: Personal blog of Hana Videen (King’s College London – also on Twitter as @OEWordhord), who posts the OE Word of the Day.

Title: Online Edition of the Épinal-Erfurt Glossary
Description: The aim of the project is to produce the first critical edition of the Épinal-Erfurt Glossary in its entirety. The project will be carried out in two phases: (1) an online edition and translation published letter by letter; (2) a printed commentary that will include discussion of the sources and the forms of both the Latin lemmata (including the Greek derivatives) and the Old English glosses. The work is being carried out at the Dictionary of Old English Project at the University of Toronto and is hosted on its website.

Title: Online Etymology Dictionary
Description: Accounts of the origin and history of English words, compiled from old dictionaries and researched from archives available online. Not designed for linguistic research.

Title: Parker Library on the Web
Description: Collection of the digital editions of the manuscripts housed in the historic Parker Library at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge.

Title: Playing with Old English: a Playful Pedagogy Resource
Description: Booklet with OE classroom activities, including instructions and printable materials, handouts, worksheets, slides. Designed within the framework of play pedagogy. Created by Megan Cavell and Renée Trilling (University of Illinois and University of Birmingham).

Title: Portable Antiquities Scheme
Description: Database recording the archaeological finds discovered by the public in England and Wales. Managed by the British Museum and the Amgueddfa Cymru - Museum Wales.

Title: Prosopography of Anglo-Saxon England (PASE)
Description: Database aiming to provide structured information relating to all the recorded inhabitants of England from the late sixth to the late eleventh century, based on a systematic examination of the available written sources for the period, including chronicles, saints’ Lives, charters, libri vitae, inscriptions, Domesday Book and coins.

Title: Regia Anglorum
Description: Nationwide re-enactment society with many independent local groups, aiming to portray all aspects of Early Medieval England life.

Title: ROEP: Resources for Old English Prose
Description: Resources for OE prose texts designed to aid researchers, instructors, and scholars at all stages. The website provides short introductions with bibliographies, translations, videos, and audio recordings, accompanied by images of the artefacts and manuscripts.Created by Francis Leneghan and Niamh Kehoe (University of Oxford).

Title: Teachers of Old English in Britain and Ireland (TOEBI)
Description: A society for everyone involved in teaching Old English in Britain and Ireland. TOEBI organizes annual conferences and publishes a newsletter.

Title: Teaching Old English in Schools
Description: Pedagogical resources for History and English teachers designed for classroom use, including worksheets and flashcards. Created by Fran Allfrey, Beth Walley, Carl Kears (King’s College, London).

Title: The Corpus of Anglo-Saxon Stone Sculpture
Description: The Corpus identifies, records, and publishes English sculpture dating from the 7th to the 11th centuries, ranging from free-standing carved crosses and decorative elements to grave-markers.

Title: The Electronic Sawyer: Online Catalogue of Anglo-Saxon Charters
Description: Digital edition of a revised, updated, and expanded version of Peter Sawyer's Anglo-Saxon Charters: an Annotated List and Bibliography, The corpus aims to provide a systematic, accurate and complete coverage of all documents falling within its scope (royal diplomas, royal writs, 'private' [non-royal] charters, vernacular documents, etc.), genuine and forged, with references to all manuscripts in which a given text has been preserved, to all published editions and translations, and to places in books or articles where any aspect of a charter is discussed (e.g. palaeography, authenticity, place-names, boundary clauses, language, formulation (diplomatic), literary interest, historical interest, witnesses, later use).

Title: The Lexis of Cloth and Clothing Project (University of Manchester)
Description: Analytical corpus of medieval dress and textiles terminology of the British Isles in the form of an illustrated database, with lexis in the early languages of Britain (Old and Middle English; Welsh, Old Irish and minor Celtic languages; Anglo-Norman/French, Medieval Latin, Anglo-Norse). The corpus investigates the origins and development of the textile/clothing vocabulary.

Title: The Medieval Monk
Description: Personal blog of Christopher Monk, who writes on the culture, texts, and everyday life of medieval England.

Title: The Old English Martyrology: An Annotated Bibliography
Description: Annotated bibliography of the Old English Martyrology with publications on all aspects of the texts, initially compiled as part of the electronic sourcing project Fontes Anglo-Saxonici (1998-99). Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: The Riddle Ages: Early Medieval Riddles, Translations and Commentaries
Description: Collection of the entire early medieval riddle tradition, including the 7th- and 8th-century Latin riddles that inspired the OE riddles, with information about the collection and texts, translations, and commentaries. The collection builds on the work from The Riddle Ages blog, active from 2013-2020, which aimed to provide Modern English translations of all the Old English riddles found in the late 10th-century Exeter Book, along with commentaries on interesting aspects of each riddle. Created by Megan Cavell (University of Birmingham) with Matthias Ammon, Neville Mogford, Jennifer Neville, Alexandra Reider and Victoria Symons.

Title: Thijs Porck Blog
Description: Personal research blog of Thijs Porck (Leiden University), who is interested in Tolkien and Early Medieval England history and culture, as well as their representations in modern scholarship and popular culture.

Title: Wordwynn: Wynsum weġ tō ealdum Englisce
Description: Textbook of basic OE grammar and vocabulary focusing on OE as a medium of everyday communication, with audio files of the lesson texts. Designed for self-learners and beginner students Created by Fritz Stieleke (Heinrich-Heine-Universität).

Title: Woruldhord
Description: Educational resources for the study of the history of Early Medieval England and OE literature and language. The archive contains photographs, documents, presentations, databases; covering objects, archaeological sites, poems, prose writings, and course material. It holds around 4,500 digital objects contributed by about 400 people or institutions, which can be freely reused for educational purposes under a Creative Commons Licence. Created by the University of Oxford.
